What are your favorite and least favorite parts of Half-Life?

EDIT: Since I can't seem to edit OP: This applies to any Half-Life game Valve has released.

I vastly prefer the parts of the game where you get human interaction directly with other people.

Parts of the game where you go for extended periods with no "human" interaction start to feel lonely.

I hate Nova Prospekt, it is a pain in the ass. But it is part of my favorite part of the game, because you have constant interaction. You have the antlions and their little quirks and funny things, which is nice and makes you feel less alone, and then you have Alyx. Between them, you are rarely alone. You have someone you can interact with beyond shooting combine soldiers.

I like most of the game post-Nova Prospekt until you get into the Citadel. You fight with other citizens and have constant help and human interaction. You get to hear other people, you get to interact and feel like you aren't alone. You aren't the one free man, the only one who can fight back. You are the one free man, the man who makes fighting back work. You take out targets, while the others help. They take out easier targets, or just provide extra damage.

I don't really like Episode 1. You feel so nerfed being limited to one weapon. After having an entire arsenal of weapons, you now have one. Don't get me wrong-- it is really fun-- but it just doesn't feel the same. I don't particularly care for the insane-ness of the Citadel either.

I really like Episode 2. You have constant interaction and collaboration with people. Sure Alyx can be annoying, but you always have someone there and talking to you. With the exception of the antlion caves, you have constant human interaction. You have Alyx, Vortigaunts, a few guys, vortigaunts, G-Man, Alyx and Vortigaunt, Alyx, and then the various staff members of BME.

I think that HL3 could totally be successful as an open world RPG. Something like Borderlands 2. You play a character, and there are story quests, and then there are sidequests to learn more about a character. I think that is totally possible. I actually prefer the more open areas.

If Valve could eliminate loading screens (No sectional loading screens like Borderlands and Skyrim, but continuous background loading like GTA), have large areas, and human interaction (which should all be possible with Source 2) I think that would be a really fun game to play. You never have to wait for "Loading..." and you always have something to do.

TL;DR: That turned into a much larger wall of text than I had planned. Read it.
